Assertions.Description: Settings Launch layout editor opens the monitor/layout surface.
The current configured physical editor shortcut opens the editor from a compatible foreground fixture.
Quick Access launches the FancyZones editor.
Disabling through Settings exits FancyZones, prevents editor hotkey activation and removes its Quick Access launch entry; enabling restores the entry and enabled grouping.
A saved collision-checked new shortcut activates the editor; the old binding does not; the restored original binding works.
Canceling a shortcut draft preserves the previously saved binding.
Quick Access shortcut Reset and Save restore working default activation without crashing the parent.
Holding a non-modifier and holding the Windows key are separate recorder conditions; neither produces abnormal blinking or unstable dialog state.
Repeated open/dismiss is safe; separately, with authorized theme switching, opening during a theme transition does not create duplicate dialogs or crash the parent.
Create an owned Unicode-named grid, save and reopen; name, type and geometry persist.
Create an owned Unicode-named canvas, save and reopen; name, type and geometry persist.
Moving an owned canvas zone changes its persisted and reopened position.
Resizing an owned canvas zone changes its persisted and reopened size.
Adding a canvas zone persists the additional zone after reopening.
Deleting a canvas zone removes only that zone after reopening.
Splitting an owned grid zone persists the split after reopening.
Merging owned grid zones persists the merged geometry after reopening.
Moving a grid edge persists resized zone geometry after reopening.
Grid Save and apply commits geometry and applies that layout to the selected work area.
Grid Cancel preserves previous geometry and assignment.
Canvas Save and apply commits geometry and applies that layout to the selected work area.
Canvas Cancel preserves previous geometry and assignment.
Deleting an owned layout removes its card and stored definition while retaining unrelated layouts.
Creating a custom copy of a template retains its geometry as an independent custom layout.
Duplicating a custom layout retains geometry with an independent identity.
Select X then right-click different Y and duplicate Y. Observe all X/Y type pairs: template/template, template/custom, custom/template, custom/custom. The copy comes from Y, not selected X.
Changed template zone count survives editor reopen and appears in layout geometry.
Changed template spacing survives editor reopen and appears between zones.
Changed template highlight distance survives editor reopen and affects adjacent-zone selection.
With two or more monitors, distinct per-monitor layouts remain independently assigned after editor reopen.
An assigned horizontal default persists and is selected as the horizontal default after reopen.
An assigned vertical default persists and is selected as the vertical default after reopen.
With multiple monitors at different DPI, each editor overlay aligns with its actual work area without shifted, clipped or wrong-monitor zones.
On an already applied custom grid, editing spacing changes the existing work area's gap without restart or reapply; observe geometry with layout-change movement enabled.
Editing an applied custom layout's highlight distance changes adjacent-zone activation on the existing work area without restart or reapply.
Adding or deleting zones on an applied custom canvas changes the active zone set without restart or reapply.
A changed highlight color is rendered in the active overlay.
A changed inactive-zone color is rendered in the overlay.
A changed border color is rendered in the overlay.
A changed zone opacity affects the rendered overlay, not merely settings readback.
Show zone number off and on separately hide and display zone numbers.
An owned executable does not snap while excluded and snaps again after its owned exclusion is removed.
Scrolling to and editing Excluded apps remains usable without repeated Settings scroll bounce.
Spanning off and on separately: Shift activation on, mouse toggle off; start drag then press Shift, observe visible zones, release Shift to hide, and separately drop while active to snap/hide.
Spanning off and on separately: Shift activation on, mouse toggle off; hold Shift before drag, observe zones, then independently verify Shift-release hide and active-drop snap/hide.
Spanning off and on separately: Shift activation off, mouse toggle on; initial zones visible, non-primary click deactivates; separately Shift deactivates.
Spanning off and on separately: Shift activation and mouse toggle off; initial zones visible, pressing Shift hides them.
Spanning off and on separately: both options on; initial zones hidden, Shift activates and non-primary click toggles the active state.
Spanning off and on separately, with two monitors: Show zones on all monitors off/on limits or displays the drag overlays accordingly.

Spanning off and on separately: unequal overlapping canvas zones honor each available overlap option (smallest, largest, positional, closest center); establish independent geometric targets for all four.
Spanning off and on separately: transparent-drag off/on retains or reduces window opacity during drag and restores the original opacity after drop and cancellation.
Spanning off and on separately: with authorized isolated empty history, a drag snap records the owned app, correct work area and zone index; retain ordinary owned-entry coverage separately.
Spanning off and on separately: with authorized isolated empty history, keyboard snapping records the owned app, correct work area and zone index; retain ordinary owned-entry coverage separately.
Spanning off and on separately: snapping to several zones records their complete correct index set.
Spanning off and on separately: unsnapping an owned single assignment removes its history record, not unrelated records.

Spanning off and on separately, with two distinct work areas where supported: snap one app on both monitors, verify both histories, unsnap one and verify the other remains. A combined work area cannot prove two independent monitor histories; retain that applicability conflict.
Spanning off and on separately, with two owned virtual desktops: snap the same app on both, unsnap one and verify only that desktop's history is removed.
Spanning off and on separately: restore-size enabled before snap and through unsnap restores the original size.
Spanning off and on separately: restore-size disabled throughout retains snapped size after unsnap.
Spanning off and on separately: restore-size disabled at snap and enabled before unsnap still retains snapped size.
Spanning off and on separately, with an authorized elevated owned target: medium-integrity PowerToys shows the privilege notification when attempting assignment.
Spanning off and on separately, with authorized elevated PowerToys and owned elevated target: assignment succeeds.
Spanning off and on separately, with an owned genuine child/tool window: enabling child snapping allows assignment.
Spanning off and on separately, using the same child-window class: disabling child snapping prevents assignment.
Spanning off and on separately: an owned window with Task View Show this window on all desktops enabled can be snapped.
Spanning off and on separately: owned app windows with Show windows from this app on all desktops enabled can be snapped.
Spanning off and on separately, with authorized display restoration: Keep windows in zones on follows changed zone bounds after resolution and scaling changes, independently.
Spanning off and on separately, with authorized display restoration: Keep windows in zones off leaves size/position unchanged after resolution and scaling changes, independently.
Spanning off and on separately, with authorized physical secondary-monitor disconnect/reconnect: an assigned window returns to its zone when the display returns.
Spanning off and on separately: with layout-change movement on, zone 1 follows new position/size between one-zone and three-zone layouts.
Spanning off and on separately: with layout-change movement on, a zone-3 window stays put when the destination layout lacks that index.
Spanning off and on separately: with layout-change movement on, a zones-1-2 window fits zone 1 on a one-zone layout.
Spanning off and on separately: after reducing zones 1-2 to zone 1, returning to the three-zone layout restores the 1-2 assignment.
Spanning off and on separately: with layout-change movement off, a zone-1 window stays put when changing layouts.
Spanning off and on separately: with last-zone placement enabled, closing/reopening an owned primary-monitor window restores its zone.
Spanning off and on separately, where distinct monitor histories exist: with history on both monitors, reopening restores the active monitor's zone.
Spanning off and on separately, where distinct monitor histories exist: with only secondary history, reopening restores the secondary zone.
Spanning off and on separately: snap, disable FancyZones, move the owned window, re-enable; the window returns to its recorded zone.
Spanning off and on separately, with secondary monitor and owned virtual desktops: an unsnapped window keeps its position/size after switching away and back.
Spanning off and on separately, with owned virtual desktops: a manually resized snapped window keeps its resized size after switching away and back.
Spanning off and on separately, with an owned genuine popup application fixture: close/reopen restores its zone.
Spanning off and on separately, in a separate owned VS Code window: menus remain anchored to controls after snapping, not relocated to the zone origin.
Spanning off and on separately, on two monitors with active-monitor placement on: a never-snapped owned window opens on the active monitor.
Spanning off and on separately: current-desktop/current-monitor history restores its zone.
Spanning off and on separately: current-desktop/other-monitor history places the new window on the active monitor.
Spanning off and on separately, with owned virtual desktops: other-desktop history places the new window on the active monitor.
Spanning off and on separately: several owned windows in one zone cycle in both previous and next shortcut directions.
Spanning off and on separately: after switching owned virtual desktops away/back, both window-cycle directions still work.
Spanning off and on separately: disabling window switching prevents both shortcuts from cycling the owned zoned windows.
Spanning off and on separately: Override Windows Snap off preserves ordinary Windows snapping without a FancyZones assignment.
Spanning off and on separately: with Zone index override, a fresh Right enters the first zone and a fresh Left enters the last, as independent conditions.
Spanning off and on separately: Left moves to previous and Right to next zone indices.
Spanning off and on separately: Up and Down retain ordinary Windows behavior in index mode.

Spanning off and on separately: retain legacy cross-monitor-off Left-at-first and Right-at-last no-zone movement requirements, but mark specification unresolved against baseline one-monitor cycling and target cycling behavior; observe both without inventing a product verdict.

Spanning off and on separately where applicable: on one physical monitor, both Left/Right wrap with cross-monitor movement enabled and disabled; spanning-on needs a multi-monitor fixture and cannot be substituted for this one-monitor condition.

Spanning off and on separately where distinct work areas apply: with multiple monitors and cross-monitor movement on, Left from first zone reaches previous monitor's last zone, including leftmost-to-rightmost wrap.
Spanning off and on separately where distinct work areas apply: Right from last zone reaches next monitor's first zone, including rightmost-to-leftmost wrap.
Spanning off and on separately: with relative-position override, each of Left/Right/Up/Down snaps a previously unsnapped window.
Spanning off and on separately: Ctrl+Alt+Win+arrows extends assignment across all zones.
Spanning off and on separately: opposite arrows reverse extension while Ctrl+Alt+Win remain held.
Spanning off and on separately: cross-monitor movement off wraps Left, Right, Up and Down within the current work area; observe every direction.
Spanning off and on separately where distinct work areas apply: cross-monitor movement on wraps Left, Right, Up and Down across the multi-monitor arrangement; observe every direction.
Spanning off and on separately: assigning different digits to owned custom layouts persists the correct mappings.
Spanning off and on separately: enabled quick switching applies each owned layout through Win+Ctrl+Alt+digit while idle.
Spanning off and on separately: enabled quick switching applies the owned layout through Win+Ctrl+Alt+digit during an active drag.

Spanning off and on separately: preserve legacy bare-digit-during-drag expectation for specification review; target releases containing the intentional modifier requirement contradict it. Do not silently score the chord as this legacy condition.
Spanning off and on separately: flash-on visibly flashes zones after switching and flash-off does not; retain both time-aware observations.
Spanning off and on separately: disabled quick switching prevents the mapped shortcuts from applying layouts.
Spanning off and on separately: disabling grid spacing produces no gap between adjacent zones during drag.
Spanning off and on separately: a newly owned virtual desktop begins with the previous desktop's layout assignments.
Spanning off and on separately: changing a new desktop's assignment and editing its applied layout are independent conditions; the other desktop's assignment/geometry remains unchanged.
Spanning off and on separately: deleting an applied owned custom layout leaves No layout assigned.

Spanning off and on separately, with authorized display restoration: an applied grid fits after resolution and scaling changes independently; absolute canvas geometry is not subject to that grid expectation.
Spanning off and on separately, only in an authorized isolated fixture after captured virtual-desktop registry/reset prerequisites: custom assignments survive lock, monitor unplug/replug and unlock.
Spanning off and on separately, only in an authorized isolated fixture after virtual-desktop registry/reset prerequisites: custom assignments survive a real computer restart.
Spanning off and on separately, only in an authorized isolated reset fixture: removing applied-layouts.json uses the chosen horizontal and vertical defaults in their respective orientations.
With two compatible monitors, spanning off produces the separate work-area layout model.
With two compatible monitors, spanning on produces the combined layout/overlay model. This does not substitute for each repeated functional child.
Normally closing an owned dragged window clears overlays/transparency; subsequent digits reach an owned input fixture and a new drag works.
Shift plus another key is not swallowed as bare Shift during drag; verify actual delivery to a compatible owned input observer.
With authorized RDP return, first no-Shift drag does not activate zones and first held-Shift drag does; no key-tap reset before observation.
With authorized sleep/wake, first no-Shift drag does not activate zones and held-Shift drag does.
With authorized lock/unlock, first no-Shift drag does not activate zones and held-Shift drag does.
Ordinary module disable/enable and authorized display/span reconfiguration during drag are separate conditions: no crash, clean overlay teardown and usable subsequent input.
With wheel switching enabled and zones visible, down selects next and up previous, including both wraparounds, on the monitor under the cursor; drop uses the selected layout.
With at least two mapped custom layouts, wheel order follows assigned digit order.
With zero assigned digits and separately one assigned digit, wheel order falls back to all custom layouts in editor order.
Wheel switching off neither changes layouts nor consumes normal wheel input.
With zones hidden, wheel input remains ordinary and does not change layouts.
With zero and with one eligible custom layout in an authorized isolated fixture, wheel input is not consumed and no layout switch occurs; two layouts is the positive control.
During visible-zone dragging, wheel and keyboard quick switches separately show the current custom layout name.
Disabling the label suppresses it; ending a drag clears an enabled label.
All seven positions apply live: top-left, top-center, top-right, center, bottom-left, bottom-center, bottom-right.
Text color and background color independently apply live and persist through Settings.
Text size and padding independently affect the rendered label live and persist through Settings.
Configured duration changes observed label lifetime and rapid switching restarts its timer; use timestamped captures without an invented exact timing tolerance.
With two monitors and ownership/authority for every processable window, holding the configured rotation chord shows numbered content previews and release dismisses them.
In the fully owned rotation fixture, Left and Right independently rotate windows in opposite directions with work-area-relative placement and coherent content numbers.
A saved new rotation chord works and the prior chord does not; restoring the original chord restores its operation.
Disabling monitor rotation prevents the chord from rotating windows.
Root and every documented subcommand help describe usable commands/options/aliases.
Canonical and alias monitor queries agree with actual monitor identities and geometry.
Canonical and alias layout queries show template and owned custom layouts with corresponding ASCII previews.
Canonical and alias active-layout queries agree with independently observed applied assignments.
Canonical and alias hotkey queries agree with independently observed mappings.
With an installed supported non-English locale, CLI help and errors localize while literal commands and options remain usable.
CLI applies a template to one selected monitor and to all monitors independently, with live geometry and persisted assignment; exercise canonical command and documented alias.
CLI applies owned grid and canvas layouts, each to one selected monitor and all monitors, with live geometry and persistence.
Quoted braced and bare custom GUID arguments from PowerShell both select the intended layout.
CLI canonical/alias set-hotkey assign a custom layout to a digit and physical activation works; remove-hotkey canonical/alias removes the assignment and activation no longer selects it.
Invalid GUID, unknown layout, invalid monitor, out-of-range digit and template-hotkey requests independently report errors without unrelated mutations.
CLI open-editor and its documented aliases open the editor.
CLI open-settings and its documented alias open the FancyZones Settings page.
With the installed PowerToys extension enabled, FancyZones editor and Settings commands each open their intended destination.
Command Palette applies owned grid and canvas layouts to one monitor and all monitors independently; previews and monitor identities agree with configuration.
After an owned layout edit and separately an authorized monitor change, revisiting shows refreshed layout/monitor data; retain the initial best-effort refresh observation.
An owned layout command can be pinned to the dock, reopened and invoked with its target preserved; remove only the owned pin and verify prior dock state.
With an installed supported non-English Windows language and authorized language restoration, editor labels/dialogs localize and Unicode layout names remain intact.
In an authorized isolated previous-version upgrade fixture, two-zone Unicode canvas and four-zone grid with one split retain settings, names and geometry.
In the isolated upgrade fixture, primary-desktop canvas and second-desktop grid assignments survive.
With two monitors in the isolated upgrade fixture, distinct per-monitor/per-desktop template assignments survive.
Authorized forced-disabled policy keeps FancyZones off after restart and prevents enabling in Settings and Quick Access.
Forced-disabled policy prevents direct editor launch with a policy log message and prevents Quick Access launch.
Authorized forced-enabled policy runs FancyZones after restart and prevents disabling in Settings and Quick Access.
With authorized conflicting computer/user policies, computer policy wins; exact original values/existence are restored.
In an isolated authorized environment with required PowerShell/DSC/WinGet, configuration.winget enables FancyZones and its physical Shift+Ctrl+Alt+F editor shortcut.
Applying the sample while PowerToys is running closes/reopens it; restore every affected module, not only FancyZones.
Applying the sample while PowerToys is stopped does not automatically reopen it.
With explicit diagnostics/viewing consent and original-state restoration, generated FancyZones utility events correspond to owned editor, CLI and snapping actions.
Inspect new FancyZones errors from the run interval and attribute them to actual actions without exposing unrelated private log content.
With an authorized real logoff/shutdown fixture, FancyZones exits without a quiesce hang; injected shutdown messages or source inspection do not substitute.
